definitions.gloss: dust; fine particles; particulate matter; airborne dust
definitions.explanation: Very small solid particles suspended in the air, often a health or safety concern in workplaces and environments.

examples.japanese: ⟦{工場|こうじょう}→工場：01082_koujou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{粉|ふん}じん⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{発生|はっせい}している→発生する：25529_hasseisuru⟧。
examples.english: Dust is being generated at the factory.

examples.japanese: {粉|ふん}じん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吸|す}い{込|こ}まない→吸い込む：06984_suikomu⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦マスク→マスク：05075_masuku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけて→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please wear a mask to avoid inhaling dust particles.

examples.japanese: ⟦{黄砂|こうさ}→黄砂：29892_kousa⟧⟦による→による：28349_niyoru⟧{粉|ふん}じん⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{濃度|のうど}→濃度：00325_noudo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}く→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦なっている→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧、⟦{外出|がいしゅつ}→外出：02543_gaishutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{控|ひか}えて→控える：10054_hikaeru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Since the dust concentration from yellow sand is high, please refrain from going outside.

notes:
Written as {粉塵|ふんじん} in full kanji or {粉|ふん}じん in mixed script (the latter is more common in general media, as {塵|じん} is not a ⟦{常用漢字|じょうようかんじ}→常用漢字：20778_jouyoukanji⟧). Refers specifically to airborne particulate matter, not everyday household dust.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {粉|ふん}じん⟦{濃度|のうど}→濃度：00325_noudo⟧ — dust concentration
- {粉|ふん}じん⟦{爆発|ばくはつ}→爆発：03575_bakuhatsu⟧ — dust explosion
- {粉|ふん}じん⟦{対策|たいさく}→対策：02511_taisaku⟧ — dust countermeasures
- {粉|ふん}じん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吸|す}い{込|こ}む→吸い込む：06984_suikomu⟧ — to inhale dust particles

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ほこり — dust (everyday household dust)
- ⟦{微粒子|びりゅうし}→微粒子：22012_biryuushi⟧ — fine particles (more scientific/technical)
- PM2.5 — fine particulate matter (specific size classification)
- ⟦{砂|すな}ぼこり→砂ぼこり：29144_sunabokori⟧ — sand dust (blown by wind)

USAGE:
A technical term commonly encountered in workplace safety regulations, environmental reports, and weather advisories (especially regarding ⟦{黄砂|こうさ}→黄砂：29892_kousa⟧ — yellow sand from China). Industrial {粉|ふん}じん exposure is regulated under Japanese occupational health laws.
